pages.text: Long ago, most people traveled by walking from place to place.
Soon, animals like horses helped carry people and goods.
Carts and wagons pulled by animals made moving heavy loads easier.
In the 1800s, steam trains began traveling on long metal tracks.
Trains could carry many passengers and goods much faster than wagons.
Later, cars powered by engines allowed families to travel on roads.
Roads expanded, connecting towns and cities across countries.
In the 1900s, airplanes began flying high above the clouds.
Air travel made it possible to cross oceans in hours instead of months.
From walking to flying, transportation changed how the world connects.
